_about: Single source for every SPAN 1001 lab page (regular semester, in-person and online). Edit this file, then run build.py. Text in *asterisks* is Spanish (rendered in italics with lang=es). Due dates are NOT stored here: build.py reads them from the lab hub's lab-due-dates.json (key SPAN1001_regular).
video_rules: Your face is visible and your voice is clear the whole time.
One notecard with up to 15 words. Don't read a script.
At the start, hold your notecard still in front of the camera for about 5 seconds, close enough to read. Don't just flash it.
No translators, AI tools, or outside help.
allowed: Class notes, your Vistas textbook, and a dictionary.
email_include: Your full name as it appears in D2L
Your course (Spanish 1001) and your professor's name
Your class days and start time, and your CRN if you know it

labs.title: Mi presentación
labs.summary: Introduce yourself: who you are, where you're from, your classes and schedule, and one person in your life.
labs.context: This is your first conversation in Spanish with your class. Answer the questions below to introduce yourself. Answer all of them, in any order, in your own words.

questions.question: *¿Qué estudias? ¿Qué eres?*
questions.guide: What do you study? What do you do (student, athlete, employee)?

questions.question: *¿Cuáles son tus clases este semestre?*
questions.guide: What are your classes this semester? Name two or three.

questions.question: *¿A qué hora es tu primera clase? ¿Y tu última clase?*
questions.guide: What time is your first class? Your last class? (Online classes: give the day and time of two events this week.)

questions.question: *¿Quién es una persona importante para ti?*
questions.guide: Who is an important person in your life? Introduce them.

questions.question: *¿De dónde es? ¿Qué estudia o qué es?*
questions.guide: Where is that person from? What do they study or do?

tips: *Soy* for yourself, *es* for the other person.
Keep *de* before a subject: *estudiante de biología*, *clase de español*.

quiz_words.intro: Ana uses these words in the video. They aren't taught until Chapter 2 or later, so you won't be tested on them. Tap a word to see what it means.

labs.title: La universidad
labs.summary: Give Andrea from Colombia a campus tour: 4 places, one slide each.
labs.context: Your friend Andrea from Colombia is visiting your university for the first time, and you are her tour guide. Make 4 slides, one for each place, and share them in Bongo while you talk.

parts.title: For each place
items: Where it is: *La biblioteca está…*
What people do there
When it's busy
Why people like it

parts.title: Across the whole video
items: 4 places on campus or nearby
At least 5 different -AR verbs
*estar* for location

rules: 4 slides, one per place (a title slide is optional)
Each slide: the place, a photo, and 3–5 Spanish keywords
No sentences on the slides. You say the sentences.
slides.bad: En la cafetería los estudiantes conversan y descansan.

hero.credit: “Now that's an admissions building!” by Chris Pesotski, Flickr, CC BY-NC-ND 2.0

labs.title: La familia
labs.summary: Introduce 3 relatives to Carmen from Mexico, one slide each.
labs.context: Introduce your family to Carmen, a friend from Mexico. Make one slide for each relative and share them in Bongo while you talk. Use a family photo, a family tree, or drawings if you prefer privacy.

parts.title: For each of at least 3 relatives
items: Who they are and their name
Their age (*tener … años*)
At least 3 adjectives that agree with the person
Where they live (*vive en…*)
What they do (*trabaja*, *estudia*, *es…*)
One more detail of your choice

rules: One slide per relative, at least 3 (a title slide is optional)
Each slide: a photo, the name, and 3–5 Spanish keywords
No sentences on the slides. You say the sentences.
slides.bad: Mi madre Ana tiene 48 años y es muy trabajadora.

words.word: Este es mi… / Esta es mi…

labs.title: Los pasatiempos
labs.summary: Your free time and a dream weekend trip, ending with a dilemma for classmates. Then a video comment.
labs.context: You're planning a dream weekend trip to a specific place in the U.S. (a named city or park, not just "the beach"). Connect your free time now to that trip, and end with a choice your classmates can help you make.

parts.title: A · Your free time now
items: What you do, where, and with whom
Use different verbs: *prefiero, quiero, puedo, vuelvo, voy*

parts.title: B · The trip
items: Where you're going, who's going, and when
At least 3 plans with *ir a* + infinitive

parts.title: C · Your dilemma
items: End with a real choice for your classmates, using *yo* and another person
*Quiero ir a las montañas, pero mi amiga prefiere la playa. ¿Qué hacemos?*

peer_points: React to their trip: would you want to go? Use *querer* or *preferir*.
Answer their dilemma: *Puedes… / Debes… / Tienes que…*
Add your own preference: *Yo prefiero… porque…*
labs.lab_images_credit: Photos from Unsplash: ben o'bro, Yu Chen Lin, Steven Abraham, Matthieu Pétiard, Marisol Benitez, Ibrahima Toure, Kevin Woblick, David Schultz, Vitaly Gariev.

labs.title: Las vacaciones
labs.summary: Be Rafa's guide to two places, say what people do there, give him tips, and end with a question for your classmates. Then a video comment.
labs.context: Rafa is visiting North Georgia for a weekend, and you're his guide. In one video, show him two real places you know. Online students can use places near where they live.

parts.title: A · Two places
items: Where each one is (*estar*): *Está cerca de…*
What each one is like (*ser*): *Es pequeño y bonito.*
*¿Qué hace la gente allí?* Two things people do: *La gente camina y come.*
One practical fact: a day, a time, or a price: *Abre a las nueve.*

parts.title: B · Tips for Rafa
items: 3 tips, with a different starter each time: *Debes…, Puedes…, Tienes que…*

parts.title: C · Your favorite
items: Which place you prefer and why: *Prefiero… porque…*
End with a question for your classmates: *¿Cuál es su lugar favorito? ¿Qué hace la gente allí?*

peer_points: Answer the question: *Mi lugar favorito es… Está en…*
Say what people do there: *La gente…*
Give the speaker one tip: *Debes ir a… / Tienes que visitar…*

hero.credit: Photo by Meg von Haartman, Unsplash

tips: *La gente* is singular: *la gente camina*, not *caminan*.
*Está* says where a place is. *Es* says what it's like.

labs.title: El repaso
labs.summary: Oral final practice: your family visits UNG for the weekend. Uses all 5 chapters.
labs.context: Your family is visiting you at UNG for the weekend, and you're planning everything. This is practice for the oral final: use as many chapters as you can.

parts.title: A · Who's visiting (Ch. 1, 3)
items: Names, relationships, and ages (*tener*)
At least 2 adjectives per person

parts.title: B · Your week (Ch. 2)
items: Your class or work schedule with -AR verbs
Where your classes are (*estar*) and when you're free

parts.title: C · Weekend plans (Ch. 4)
items: At least 3 plans with *ir a* + infinitive
*quiero, prefiero, podemos, volvemos*

parts.title: D · Where everyone is staying (Ch. 5)
items: Conditions and feelings with *estar*: *El hotel está limpio. Estamos contentos.*
Something someone is doing right now: *Mi mamá está buscando un restaurante.*

checklist: *ser* for who people are and what they're like
quiz_topics: Two short videos, each with its own questions
quiz_rules: Use only the information from that section's video.
Write verbs in the present tense.
Write numbers as words, not digits.
Fill-in-the-blank: use the exact words from the video. Spelling counts.
Select all that apply: choose every correct option.

proposal.lead: Same six labs, same Bongo recordings. Students find everything in one place, test their setup before the first lab, and are graded on one speaking rubric.
now: Labs live in a Start Here module plus 6 subfolders, with 3–4 pages of instructions per lab
Pages sometimes disagree (how many places in Lab 2, one or two videos in Lab 5)
Labs are due on Fridays at 3:00 PM
Students first find out their setup can't record on a due date
No face or no audio: Incomplete the first time, then 0
Rubric with an Engagement row that fits only Labs 4–5, and no vocabulary row
proposed: One LAB folder: a short description, the Guidelines Quiz, Lab 0, then each lab's quiz and recording. Instructions live inside Bongo
One set of instructions, so the details always match
Labs are due at {DUE_TIME}, as in SPAN 1002
Lab 0 in the first week: a one-minute camera + screen check that unlocks the labs
No face or no audio: 0, no resubmission, as in SPAN 1002
One speaking rubric (25 points) with a vocabulary row and a 0 column
Students type accented words in the Guidelines Quiz, and an accent bar sits inside the quizzes
notice: A clear start: the announcement walks them through 4 steps, with buttons to the LAB folder and the Guidelines Quiz.
Simpler Bongo pages: the task, the rules and the recording steps on one page, with tabs for vocabulary and troubleshooting.
Help for their kind of lab: Troubleshooting is split into video labs and slide labs, with one fallback for each: a phone or camera-app take, or a PowerPoint or Canva MP4.

Clear responsibility: students make sure their recording works and is in the right format. No late labs, including for technology problems reported before the due time. Students with an Excused Absence tell the Lab within 2 business days, and every make-up closes 7 days after the due date.
tasks: Lab 2: a campus tour of 4 places, one slide each.
Lab 3: at least 3 relatives, one slide each.
Labs 4–5: students watch one classmate's video and leave a video comment.
Lab 5: one video: a North Georgia tour for Rafa with tips, using Chapters 1–4 only, so it works before Chapter 5 is taught.
Recording in the Lab: optional for in-person sections. Online sections record on their own and can book online tutoring.
same: 6 labs, 25 points each, graded by Language Lab staff.
Each lab is a mini-quiz plus a Bongo recording, 1.5–2 minutes, face visible, Spanish only.
No late work apart from Excused Absences. The Guidelines Quiz (75%) still unlocks the labs, now together with Lab 0.
